title: POC weekly sync - rollout / go-live planning
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Johnson (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Tom Rivera (GreenLeaf PM), Maria Chen (GreenLeaf Platform Eng), Sana Iqbal (GreenLeaf Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout and go-live planning for the inference POC. Reviewed canary strategy, cutover steps, monitoring/alerts, security signoffs, and outstanding tuning items. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide runbook and canary dashboard, GreenLeaf to validate thresholds and complete security checklist, schedule canary for 2027-01-12 pending infra prep.
action_items: Tom Rivera: validate canary metrics thresholds (latency p95, error rate) and share Grafana dashboard link (due: 2027-01-05)
Priya Desai (Redwood): produce step-by-step cutover runbook and night-of checklist (due: 2027-01-07)
Maria Chen: confirm VPC peering & firewall rules for dedicated test subnet and provide IP allowlist (due: 2027-01-04)
Sana Iqbal: complete SOC2/ISO checklist verification and send any remaining questions (due: 2027-01-06)
Alex Johnson: share small pricing/commitment worksheet for canary capacity and burst plan (due: 2027-01-03)
next_steps: Redwood to circulate cutover runbook and canary measurement dashboard by Jan 7
GreenLeaf to complete infra prep and share dashboard by Jan 5
Agree on canary start window: tentative 2027-01-12 02:00-06:00 UTC
Schedule final pre-cutover sync 2027-01-10 to confirm readiness
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Johnson: hey everyone thanks for joining, I see Tom, Maria, Sana and Priya on. quick agenda — canary plan, cutover steps, monitoring, security, and open items.
[00:12] Tom Rivera: yep thanks Alex, excited — we had last week's perf numbers, latency looks decent but p95 spikes with long prompts. Maria dug in a bit.
[00:25] Maria Chen: yeah so on our side the long tail is the issue, we see p95 at ~620ms during the big batch, average is fine. also kv cache hit rate is lower than expected for some routes.
[00:38] Priya Desai: okay, that matches what we saw on Redwood logs — KV cache warmup is the main factor; we recommended prefix caching for the high-frequency prompts and a small pre-warm job before the canary window.
[00:52] Tom Rivera: can you quantify the pre-warm? like how long and how many requests?
[00:58] Priya Desai: roughly 10k quick prefix requests over 5-10 minutes for the traffic cohort; we can script that — Redwood can provide the script.
[01:10] Alex Johnson: good — action: Redwood provides script. moving on to canary thresholds. what metrics do we want to gate on?
[01:21] Tom Rivera: p95 latency, 99th maybe for safety, error rate, and key correctness checks — like top-3 model outputs match our golden set for 95% of requests.
[01:33] Maria Chen: on infra side we also want CPU/GPU utilization alerts and queue length to know if batching backlog builds.
[01:41] Sana Iqbal: and from security, we need audit logging validated, KMS integration verified, and confirm data retention settings for the pilot. also SSO for SRE on both sides.
[01:54] Alex Johnson: ok, Redwood supports acoustic audit logs and KMS integration — Priya can share our security doc and the SSO config.
[02:03] Priya Desai: yes I'll send the security checklist and a short runbook for the KMS flow. note: sometimes the transcription of the KMS name gets messy — it's customer-managed K-M-S with the usual key rotation options.
[02:18] Tom Rivera: on rollback criteria: if p95 increases by 30% from baseline or error rate > 0.5% for five minutes, we want an automatic rollback to previous model variant. is that feasible?
[02:30] Priya Desai: yes, Redwood can configure canary with automatic fallback to a pinned variant. we just need to confirm the exact thresholds and the monitoring hooks.
[02:40] Alex Johnson: great — we'll outline the exact thresholds in the runbook. next, cutover timing and who owns each step. Tom, do you want the canary to run during low traffic overnight?
[02:52] Tom Rivera: yes, target is low-traffic window; tentatively Jan 12 in our timezone is fine, looks like 02:00-06:00 UTC works.
[03:02] Maria Chen: we'll need at least 48 hours to open firewall rules and test peering on our staging subnet to mimic prod.
[03:10] Alex Johnson: understood — Maria will confirm by Jan 4. Priya, can you confirm the number of instances for the canary cluster?
[03:19] Priya Desai: for the initial canary we recommend 3 instances with burst to 6 if the workload is heavier; we can set autoscale thresholds and cap burst to control cost.
[03:31] Tom Rivera: what's the expected cost delta for a 4-hour canary vs normal? we need to estimate for finance.
[03:37] Alex Johnson: I'll send the small pricing worksheet; rough ballpark is X for the reserved + spike capacity, but we'll put concrete numbers in the doc.
[03:47] Sana Iqbal: security question — will logs that contain PII be redacted before leaving our VPC? we need to ensure no sensitive fields are batched to Redwood hosted logs.
[03:58] Priya Desai: Redwood supports field-level redaction and options to keep logs inside your private deployment; for hosted we'll provide configurable scrubbing and the option to disable retention. we'll include this in the security doc.
[04:12] Maria Chen: on monitoring, can Redwood provide a Grafana dashboard reference with the p50/p95/p99, error counts, KV hit rate, queue length, and a health check? that would speed our validation.
[04:23] Priya Desai: yes we can deliver a dashboard template and a short Prometheus exporter config. we'll share a link to a demo dashboard.
[04:34] Tom Rivera: perfect, once we have the dashboard we'll set the thresholds and run an internal smoke test.
[04:40] Alex Johnson: recap — Redwood provides runbook, pre-warm script, canary dashboard, security checklist, and pricing sheet by Jan 7 (except pricing by Jan 3). GreenLeaf completes infra and thresholds by Jan 5. Pre-cutover sync Jan 10. Canary target window Jan 12.
[04:58] Tom Rivera: sounds good. one more thing — model quality checks, we want automated rerank checks during the canary to detect regressions. can that be added as a gate?
[05:09] Priya Desai: yes, we can wire in a lightweight rerank/eval step against a small test corpus and fail the gate if similarity drops beyond the threshold. we'll include that in the runbook.
[05:19] Alex Johnson: okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs. meeting adjourned.
notes: Reference artifacts mentioned: Redwood runbook (link TBD), canary dashboard demo (link TBD), pricing worksheet (link TBD). Some transcription artifacts: 'KMS' sometimes spelled K-M-S or kms, 'kv cache' appears as 'k v cache' occasionally.
